questions.question: For the tree with root 1, children 2 and 3, where 2 has children 4 and 5 and 3 has a right child 6, what is the inorder traversal?
questions.explanation: Inorder visits left subtree, node, right subtree: 4 2 5, then 1, then 3 6. The other options are preorder, postorder and level order.

questions.question: What is the space complexity of recursive DFS on a binary tree of height h?
options: O(w), where w is the widest level
questions.explanation: The recursion holds one frame per level on the current path, so O(h): O(log n) for a balanced tree and O(n) for a skewed one. O(w) describes BFS.

questions.question: Why is the diameter computed inside the same recursive height function rather than by calling height() separately at every node?
options: Because the diameter always passes through the root
Because separate height calls would recompute subtrees and make it O(n²) instead of O(n)
Because JavaScript does not allow nested functions
Because height must be counted in edges
questions.explanation: Computing heights bottom-up once and updating a running best at each node visits every node once, keeping the solution O(n).

questions.question: Which traversal is naturally implemented with a queue and processes the tree level by level?
questions.explanation: Breadth-first (level-order) traversal uses a queue so nodes are processed in order of depth; DFS orders use recursion or a stack.
